newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine teachers strike after woman shot in riots.
newsitem.headline: Argentine teachers strike after woman shot in riots.

text.p: Argentine teachers held a nationwide strike on Monday to protest the death of a young woman in a rally in the southern province of Neuquen that turned into a pitched battle with paramilitary police.

The walkout by teachers in state schools was massive across the country in honour of Teresa Rodriguez, 24, who died from a gunshot wound on Saturday. The mother of three was passing by on her way to work when she was shot in the neck.
"The sole cause of this strike is the death of a comrade in Cutral-Co and the repression," said Marta Maffei, head of the national teachers' union CTERA.

Witnesses and unions blamed the death on gendarmes flown to the oil towns of Cutral-Co and Plaza Huincul to break up a highway blockade by striking teachers and control Saturday's protest of more than 10,000 teachers and local residents.
Interior Minister Carlos Corach, fending off calls for his resignation and that of Education Minister Susana Decibe, said the shot that killed Rodriguez was not fired by police.

"The gendarmes were attacked with molotov cocktails and shots were heard," an angry Corach told reporters on Monday. "What must be condemned, apart from the unfortunate death of this young woman, is the use of violence and blockades of roads, the destruction of private property and stances that put people's lives in danger."

As smaller skirmishes continued and unions and opposition parties heeded the union's call for stoppages and a march through Buenos Aires on Monday, Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez blamed it all on the centre-left coalition Frepaso.

"Everyone knows which party the union leaders who led the protests in Cutral-Co belong to, and that is the Frepaso, which talks of democracy but doesn't respect the principles of democracy," the Peronist government official said.
Neuquen teachers have been on strike for a month against 20 percent pay cuts but are near a deal with the province to include half-pay for each day out if they get back to work.
The teachers' ranks have been swollen by poor locals in an oil-drilling area where the privatisation of state oil giant YPF five years ago left thousands jobless.
